scopeReview: PSO-1.B.1–2: sustainability, resources, land use and the evolution from environmental determinism to possibilism. Original hypothetical examples avoid ranking real societies or equating climate with human capability.
varietyReview: Resource balance, cover-change chart, upstream/downstream map, controlled comparison and seven distinct applied concepts. Four stimuli, all key positions and varied difficulty; no externally sourced statistics or images.
repetitionReview: Distinct from prior spatial-data topics: focuses on environmental constraints, choices, modification, resource valuation and sustainability. Similar-setting comparison and the aridity critique distinguish evidence interpretation from theory application rather than repeating the same stem.

questions.correctOption: The proposal draws down storage by 40 million m³ per year under the stated assumptions.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed the mass balance independently: recharge100 minus current90=+10; recharge100 minus proposed140=−40 million m³/year. Initial storage is absent, excluding an exact depletion date.

questions.correctOption: Forest area declined while cropland and built-up area increased.
questions.independentReview: Independently summed both inventories to100 km² and differences−30,+10,+20. Conservation of total area holds, but aggregate margins cannot identify each source-to-destination land conversion.

questions.correctOption: Runoff generated in the heavily paved western area may travel toward the eastern area.
questions.independentReview: Checked arrow endpointx90>startx10, west80% vs east20%, and upstream-to-downstream connection. The supplied infiltration premise supports a hypothesis, not a guaranteed flood or quantified discharge.

questions.correctOption: Similar physical conditions can coexist with different land uses when access to technology differs.
questions.independentReview: Compared the controlled scenario fields: rainfall500 mm and similar soils/terrain, but irrigation accessYes/No and cropsvegetables/drought-tolerant grains. This is a counterexample to a unique climate-determined practice, not a proof of unlimited technological control.

questions.correctOption: Water constraints matter, but technology, institutions and connections can produce different responses.
questions.independentReview: Assessed the universal wordmust against alternative feasible responses; correct option retains constraint plus agency, unlike the three absolute denials or equivalences. No real group is stereotyped.

questions.correctOption: Technology expands some possibilities, while energy costs and waste-management requirements remain relevant.
questions.independentReview: Checked the distinction between expanded feasibility and eliminated constraints. The question assumes a functioning system, not universal affordability, zero waste or a climate-fixed policy.

questions.correctOption: Human uses and technology help determine which environmental materials are treated as resources.
questions.independentReview: Independently separated physical stock from social/economic valuation. Only usefulness changes in the scenario; quantity creation and impact-free extraction are unsupported.

questions.correctOption: Long-term maintenance, ecological outcomes and effects on residents’ housing and livelihoods
questions.independentReview: Checked that the answer expands the specified incomplete assessment without prescribing an unsupported policy. Housing/livelihood consequences matter because relocation is explicit, not assumed.

questions.correctOption: Land cover describes the surface, while land use describes its human purpose.
questions.independentReview: Tested two possible uses with identical vegetation: sports and grazing. The counterexample establishes why cover alone is insufficient to uniquely classify purpose.

questions.correctOption: The environmental connection can transmit effects beyond the administrative area where the activity occurs.
questions.independentReview: Followed the explicit river pathway across boundaries. The correct inference concerns relevant extent, not an unmeasured amount of farm damage or a claim that every discharge reaches every farm.

questions.correctOption: People respond to a physical constraint while also modifying the landscape.
questions.independentReview: Checked both directions of influence: slope motivates adaptation; construction changes surface form. Neither physical inevitability nor independence is supported.
